subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Differential Gears: Splitting Power
description: A 60-second lesson on Differential Gears: Splitting Power.

hook.text: In a turn, the outer wheel travels farther than the inner one.

buildup.text: A differential uses bevel gears to split torque between two outputs.

discovery.text: Both wheels get equal torque but can spin at different speeds.

twist.text: If one wheel is on ice, all torque goes to it — and you're stuck.

climax.text: Limited-slip differentials fix this by forcing some torque to the gripping wheel.

punchline.text: The differential solved turning. The limited-slip solved ice.

quiz.question: Why does a standard differential cause problems on ice?
options: Both wheels lock up and the car slides straight
All torque goes to the wheel with least grip, so neither wheel pushes
The differential overheats from spinning the ice-bound wheel
